commit.message:
Disable yield-local optimization for sticky VTs, use local+signal for start

The yield optimization (!stickyAffinity gate in afterYield) kept sticky VTs
on the carrier's local FJP queue after Thread.yield(), even when the queue
was empty. This trapped carriers inside topLevelExec (avg 52 tasks/1.25ms
per entry vs 1.7 tasks/0.037ms without), starving external queue scanning.
Handler VT I/O wait times increased from 32ms to 52-71ms.

Revert the yield path to upstream fibers behavior: all VTs (including
sticky) go to the external queue when the local queue is empty.

Change the start path from lazySubmit to pool.execute for sticky callers.
This preserves local queue placement (good for locality) while adding
conditional signaling (good for parallelism on 2-core configs).
